process_type: Atomic Layer Deposition (ALD) and Electron Beam Evaporation
summary: The study investigates the resistive switching properties of NiO and Nb2O5 films deposited by electron beam evaporation and atomic layer deposition (ALD). The films are used as resistive switching materials for ReRAM devices, with a focus on their structural, chemical, and electrical characteristics. The research highlights the impact of deposition techniques and electrode materials on the performance of these films.
evidence: NiO films are grown using two different techniques: atomic layer deposition (ALD) and electron beam evaporation. NiO films (10–80 nm thick) are deposited by ALD on n+-Si(100) and metal substrates (Pt, W, and TiN) in the ASM F-120 reactor using the Ni(C5H5)2 and O3 precursor combination at 300 /C176C. Electron beam evaporation of 10–160 nm thick NiO films is performed on n+-Si, Pt, W, and TiN substrates starting from NiO pellets with 3–6 mm diameter and 99.9% purity. The deposition rate is around 4–5 nm/min and the growth temperature is 40–50 /C176C.
